To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the expression levels of the VP1 and 2A genes of EV71 are higher than the other capsid genes, and that the expression levels are higher in the brain tissue than in the spinal cord and the peripheral blood of patients.
the expression of VP1-VP2-VP3-VP4 of EV71 can be inhibited by shRNAs targeting VP1-VP3- VP4 genes of EV71, which can inhibit EV71 replication.
shRNAs targeting VP1,VP2 and VP3 genes showed inhibitory effect on EV71 replication and the effects could further be enhanced when used in combination.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study on the mechanism of EV71 infection in vitro and the development of a new antiviral strategy.
the development of a novel and efficient method to produce recombinant lentivirus for gene therapy.
the development of a novel method to produce a large number of recombinant EV71 VP2 protein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of shRNA targeting viral capsomeres is a promising therapeutic approach to inhibit EV71 infection.
the study is well designed, and the data are convincing.

the use of a combination of shRNAs against the capsomeres of VP1, VP2, VP3, and VP4 of EV71 could be a promising therapeutic strategy to inhibit the viral replication and reduce the viral load in EV71 infection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have successfully established a new method for the preparation of the recombinant EV71 VP4 proteins and the recombinant VP4 protein can be expressed at a high level in E.coli and can be used as an antigen for the development of a new diagnostic method for EV71.
the inhibitory effects on enterovirus71 replication of shRNA targeting VP1-VP2-VP3-VP4 genes are all over 50% and can be enhanced by using shRNAs together.
we have developed a series of shRNA vectors targeting VP1, VP2, VP3, and VP4 genes of EV71, which can inhibit EV71 replication in vitro.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have shown that shRNAs targeting VP1-VP3 of EV71 can be used alone or in combinations to inhibit EV71 replication.
the shRNAs used in the study could be applied as a potential treatment for EV71 infections.
we have developed a new method for the detection of EV71 infection.
